sections.overview: The short-beaked echidna is an Australian egg-laying mammal, or monotreme.
sections.identification: It has a long snout, short limbs and a spiny back.
sections.habitat: It occurs throughout Australia, including Tasmania, in habitats from woodland and heath to grassland and arid country.
sections.diet: It opens ant and termite nests and catches prey with its sticky tongue.
sections.behavior: Its claws help it dig into insect nests.
sections.reproduction: One egg is laid and hatches after about 10 days; the young suckles in the pouch, then in a burrow.
sections.ecology: By feeding on ants and termites, it is an insectivore adapted to forage in nests and soil.
sections.conservation: It remains widespread but is less common in Sydney than before, according to the Australian Museum.
